REUTERS/Stringer July 21 (Reuters) - A Liberian-flagged vessel sailing from Egypt to Ukraine has been hit ‌off Romania's coast in an attack likely ‌linked to Russia's war on Ukraine, Romanian President Nicusor Dan ​said on Tuesday. This year, Russian and Ukrainian drones have repeatedly breached the airspace and territorial waters of Romania, officials in the European Union and ‌NATO member state ⁠neighbouring Ukraine have said. "Last night, the LPG Gas Lisbon, a Liberian-flagged vessel, was ⁠hit outside Romanian territorial waters, approximately 20 nautical miles (40 km) off the Romanian coast," Dan wrote ​on X. Advertisement Advertisement Dan ​said Romanian rescuers had ​evacuated the crew, including ‌three injured members, and a tugboat had been dispatched to ensure the vessel did not drift and pose a danger to navigation. "State institutions are on alert and will clarify the circumstances, ‌causes and responsibilities related to ​this serious incident, most likely ​part of the ​illegal war of aggression of the ‌Russian Federation against Ukraine," Dan ​said. Russia, which ​launched a full scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, has either denied responsibility for reported ​attacks on ‌Romania, said they were carried out by ​Ukraine, or blamed Ukrainian "provocation". Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha greeted the delegations, which included Estonian PM Kristen Michal, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Latvian PM Andris Kulbergs, Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre, and Danish PM Mette Frederiksen. by Kyiv Post | Aug. 23, 2026, 1:03 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha and Finnish President Alexander Stubb arrive in Kyiv on Aug. 23. (Photo: Andriy Sybiha/X) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Leaders from six European nations arrived in Kyiv on the morning of Sunday, Aug. 23, to participate in commemorations for Ukraine’s Flag Day and Independence Day, as well as a series of high-level diplomatic meetings. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andri Sybiha announced that he greeted the leaders of Denmark , Estonia , Finland , Latvia , Lithuania , and Norway at the Kyiv railway station. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “On the eve of Independence Day, we feel that we are not alone. Our allies are by our side,” Sybiha wrote on X. “They will hold bilateral and multilateral talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky . Important decisions will be made and important statements will be issued.” Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also confirmed his arrival on X, noting the shared history of Estonia and Ukraine restoring their independence 35 years ago. Advertisement “[Russian President Vladimir] Putin hopes that time is on his side. Our task is to prove him wrong,” Michal wrote. “Ukraine must have everything necessary to defend itself and decide its future independently.” Finnish President Alexander Stubb arrived for a two-day visit accompanied by his wife, Suzanne Innes-Stubb, according to the Finnish broadcaster YLE . The Finnish delegation also includes the Commander of the Defense Forces, Janne Jaakkola, and a group of entrepreneurs. Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is also among the visiting delegation. According to the Baltic news outlet BB.lv , Kulbergs emphasized Latvia’s determination to help Ukraine prepare for the upcoming winter. Other Topics of Interest Ukraine: What is Driving the Push for Elections? Reactions in the European press to a call for elections in wartime Ukraine from a popular, abruptly dismissed, defense minister. Before arriving in the capital, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre condemned the recent wave of Russian strikes across Ukraine. “Russia has no remorse when it comes to distinguishing between civilian and military targets,” Støre stated. “It is precisely civilian infrastructure, residential buildings, schools, and hospitals that have suffered, which is a systematic violation of international law.” Advertisement Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen also commented on the recent Russian attacks, emphasizing the necessity of continued support for Ukraine. Ahead of our Independence Day, we feel we are not alone. Our allies are with us. Today in the morning, I was pleased to welcome leaders of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, alongside other high representatives, at the Kyiv Railway Station. They will hold… pic.twitter.com/NmPgIVH1g3 — Andrii Sybiha 🇺🇦 (@andrii_sybiha) August 23, 2026 Diplomatic summits and allied support The visiting leaders are scheduled to participate in a series of events over the next two days, including the national holiday commemorations and bilateral meetings with President Zelensky. The officials will also take part in a summit of the NB8 (Nordic-Baltic Eight) format, which brings together the five Nordic and three Baltic states. Additionally, the leaders are expected to attend a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, a group coordinating international support for Ukraine, which is scheduled to convene in Kyiv on Monday, Aug. 24. The arrival of the Nordic and Baltic leaders follows the earlier arrival of Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda , who announced on Sunday morning that he would also be participating in the NB8 discussions and the Coalition of the Willing meeting. https://www.dw.com/en/elon-musk-ordered-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OUWh Ukraine has accused Elon Musk's SpaceX of restricting Starlink service in the country [FILE: May 30, 2025] Image: Nathan Howard/REUTERS Advertisement Tech billionaire Elon Musk ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on , the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials. Kyiv uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations . Restricting the service means restricting the country's attack and defense missions against Russia. Last week, Musk capped the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network, the report said, citing unnamed sources. The move rendered some offensive drones and interceptor drones virtually useless, it added. Two people told the Journal that Musk and US President Donald Trump discussed the Starlink decision in a call soon after the slowdown became public. Some US officials, the report said, believed Musk acted unilaterally and that Trump did not specifically order retribution against Ukraine. However, one person familiar with the situation said Musk spoke with multiple senior administration officials, including Trump, before imposing the speed cap. Both Musk and Trump have expressed anger at Ukraine for attacking Russian diesel refineries in recent weeks , which the president blames for high energy prices. The report also comes after Trump's comments last week that he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access. Musk had said that any limits on speed or use were decided by the US military or the president. Musk, SpaceX, and the White House are yet to respond to the report. US envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday after what a US official called "constructive" talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway , as Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war .
